title: How Lovable self-improves every hour — Benjamin Verbeek, Lovable

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling

summary: Benjamin Verbeek from Lovable presents the platform's two continuous improvement loops at scale. Lovable, which coined 'vibe coding,' serves primarily non-technical users via a chat interface and now creates over 200,000 projects per day. The first loop addresses solvable stuck states: an LLM judge flags sessions showing repeated requests, complaints, or abandonment. When a stuck user eventually succeeds, the system identifies what context should have been injected upfront, clusters similar issues to avoid overfitting, and an external reviewer agent validates solutions via quick evals. Validated context is injected into future sessions, with a holdout group receiving blank injections to measure real project completion impact. Effective entries are shown more; harmful or stale ones are pruned—essential because knowledge rots quickly when models or features change. The second loop addresses unsolvable problems: Lovable gave the agent a 'vent tool' to complain directly to creators via Slack when tooling, docs, or platform behavior degrades its work. Unlike an external reviewer forced to comment every iteration (low signal-to-noise, overfitting to noise), the vent tool fires only on genuine frustration, yielding high signal. The agent has far more context than the user about the root cause. Early wins include catching a silent copy-tool bug with spaces in filenames—20 complaints in the first hour—and discovering non-breaking spaces from WhatsApp/Mac screenshots also broke the tool. Vent volume spikes turned out to be a reliable incident detector. A second agent now monitors the channel, deduplicates reports, investigates, and automatically opens PRs, with developers reviewing and merging. The team is working to fully close the loop: detect shortcomings, merge fixes, and continuously evaluate.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction & Background
sections.summary: Verbeek introduces himself, his physics background (satellites, particle physics, fusion reactors), and the talk's theme: continuous learning at scale—learning from mistakes so they happen once and never again.

sections.title: Lovable Interface & Vibe Coding
sections.summary: Lovable coined 'vibe coding'—building software via a chat interface and model sandbox without looking at code. Users stick to one project for a long time, enabling detailed user understanding. Lovable builds for the 99% who cannot code.

sections.title: Scale & Growth Journey
sections.summary: Lovable grew from a few thousand users to over 200,000 projects per day in about a year. Scaling was fun but hard—GitHub banned them on day one for too many repos, and they took down cloud providers.

sections.title: The Stuck Problem: Technical vs Non-Technical Users
sections.summary: Technical users hit friction but work past it; non-technical users hit technical blocks and give up, never experiencing successful AI. Lovable's goal is to ensure no user gets permanently stuck.

sections.title: Detecting & Categorizing Stuck States
sections.summary: An LLM judge flags stuck sessions by detecting repeated requests, complaints about failed implementations, and abandoned sessions. Stuck states split into solvable-with-prompting and unsolvable; unsolvable breaks into easy fixes (bugs, simple additions) and hard engineering problems.

sections.title: Stack Overflow for Lovable
sections.summary: When a stuck user eventually succeeds, the system identifies what context should have been injected upfront. Similar issues are clustered to avoid overfitting. An external reviewer agent runs quick evals to validate solutions, creating a continually updated knowledge bank.

sections.title: Holdout Validation, Pruning & Results
sections.summary: A holdout group receives blank injections to compare completion rates. Effective entries are shown more; harmful ones pruned. Knowledge becomes stale rapidly with new models or features, so continuous rebalancing is critical. Results show significant drops in stuck messages and increased deployments; all top internal models use Stack Overflow context.

sections.title: The Vent Tool: Agent Feedback to Creators
sections.summary: For unsolvable problems, Lovable gave the agent a vent tool to complain directly to Slack when tooling, docs, or platform behavior degrades its work. Unlike external reviewers forced to comment every iteration (low signal-to-noise, overfit to noise), the vent tool fires only on genuine frustration. The agent has far more context than the user about root causes.

sections.title: Vent Tool Examples & Copy Bug Discovery
sections.summary: Examples include agent complaints about Framer Motion TypeScript types and a silent copy-tool bug where filenames with spaces failed—20 complaints in the first hour. Non-breaking spaces from WhatsApp/Mac screenshots also broke the regex. The team fixed it iteratively until the issue never recurred.

sections.title: Vent Flow, Incident Detection & Automated PRs
sections.summary: Vent messages go to Slack. A second agent now monitors, deduplicates, investigates, and opens PRs automatically; developers review and merge. Vent volume spikes reliably detected incidents like broken sandboxes. The agent even gave meta-feedback that the vent tool was too easy to trigger. The team aims to fully close the detect-fix-eval loop.

demonstrations: Vent tool example: agent complains about Framer Motion TypeScript types requiring unnecessary casting for a simple cubic bezier
Copy tool bug: agent reported file copy failing when filenames contained spaces; 20 complaints in first hour; fix revealed non-breaking spaces from WhatsApp/Mac screenshots also broke the regex
Meta feedback: agent complained the vent tool was too easy to trigger and it couldn't retract messages, being 'ashamed' of what it sent

Example stuck session: user complains about laggy scrolling, agent fails multiple times, eventually identifies overlay text individual gradients as cause, stuck flag resets—becomes a Stack Overflow knowledge entry
